watch_items.text: Watch for the first public polling with Jackson as the named Democratic nominee, and whether Republicans successfully tie him to the Platner allegations in paid media over the next two weeks. Also watch whether Sanders modifies or continues defending his original Platner endorsement — continued defiance is a usable attack line.
watch_items.title: Maine Senate race, Jackson vs. Collins

watch_items.text: Watch for FDA or CDC confirmation of containment status and any documentation (leaked or FOIA'd) of communications between Taylor Farms and the White House regarding recall timing. This is the highest-value accountability thread in this set and is currently thin on reporting.
watch_items.title: Taylor Farms recall/outbreak

watch_items.text: Watch for whether "abolish the Senate" or similar structural-reform rhetoric gets amplified by national DSA chapters or picked up by Democratic primary challengers — this is the kind of proposal that becomes a general-election attack ad regardless of how marginal it is within DSA itself.
watch_items.title: DSA internal messaging

watch_items.text: Watch for any independent verification (court records, local reporting) of the "260 arrests, all with criminal records" claim. Self-reported enforcement statistics from DHS/ICE have a documented history of later requiring correction.
watch_items.title: ICE Houston operation follow-up

top_cluster.headline: Maine Democrats nominated state Senate leader Troy Jackson to replace Graham Platner, who dropped his Senate campaign amid sexual assault allegations, setting up a race against Republican incumbent Susan Collins that both parties view as pivotal to control of the Senate.
top_cluster.left_framing: Center-left outlets (NPR) treat Jackson's nomination as a routine, almost reassuring succession story, foregrounding his legislative résumé and downplaying the scandal that forced Platner out; Politico separately emphasizes the scale of the Republican counter-offensive against him, implicitly casting Jackson as a serious threat worth attacking.
top_cluster.center_framing: Center outlets (Axios, The Hill) situate the Maine race within the broader 100-days-to-midterms horse-race narrative, weighing favorable Democratic polling signals against structural Republican advantages in the Senate map, without focusing on Maine's candidate-specific scandal at all.
top_cluster.right_framing: Far-right coverage (Breitbart) leads with the sexual assault allegations against Platner and highlights Sanders' unapologetic continued support for him, using the episode as evidence of Democratic Party dysfunction, while still conceding Jackson may have a strong chance of winning.
top_cluster.left_omissions: Left-leaning coverage omits or softens the specifics of the sexual assault allegations against Platner and does not mention Sanders' unrepentant stance on his earlier endorsement, details that right-leaning coverage foregrounds.
top_cluster.right_omissions: Right-leaning (Breitbart) coverage omits Jackson's own political background and legislative experience, the scale/sophistication of the Republican campaign being mounted against him (per Politico), and the broader headwinds — Trump's approval ratings and economic frustration — that other outlets say are weighing on Republican Senate chances.
